subject: SLA & multi-site failover capabilities for isolated/private deployment
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice@lumenhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@lumenhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment SLA / failover questions

Irene —

Thanks for taking our RFP. A couple of follow-ups from the architecture team as we scope our procurement: can you provide definitive answers for the private (VPC/on‑prem/air‑gapped) deployment options around the following?

- Minimum SLA you will commit to for a single isolated deployment (uptime %, maintenance windows)
- Options for multi‑site failover: active/active, active/passive, cold standby — which do you support out of the box vs. via customization?
- Expected RTO / RPO targets for each failover mode
- Network assumptions (outbound egress, NAT traversal, cross‑site heartbeat) for air‑gapped sites
- Operational runbook for operator failover (who performs what steps, estimated time)

If you can send a one‑page summary plus a technical appendix we can include in the RFP binder that would be ideal. Also let me know if you need our network diagrams.

Best,
Alice
Alice Park
Senior Infrastructure Architect — LumenHealth
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA / failover questions

Hi Alice —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick summary up front: Redwood supports both active/passive and active/active topologies for private deployments; for fully air‑gapped installs we follow an explicit operator‑driven failover model (automated cross‑site orchestration requires a secured control plane connection and is available where networking permits).

I've attached our SLA matrix and the operator failover runbook (high level) — they cover uptime commitments, maintenance windows, and the default RTO/RPO targets by topology. Key points:

- Single‑site isolated deployment SLA: 99.9% uptime monthly (standard), 99.95% available with reserved capacity contract and documented maintenance windows.
- Active/passive failover (supported): typical RTO 5–30 minutes (automated orchestration + cold cache rebuild); RPO depends on KV cache persistence config (default: near‑zero for stateful checkpoints; for stateless workloads RPO ≈ 0).
- Active/active (supported with network peering): near‑zero RTO for stateless routing; for KV cache coherence we recommend eventual consistency with cross‑site async replication — RPO typically < 1 minute with our recommended config.
- Air‑gapped sites: operator‑initiated failover procedure in runbook (human trigger + scripted steps). RTO target for air‑gapped operator failover: 30–120 minutes depending on dataset size and operator readiness.

Notes on networking and assumptions:
- For air‑gapped installs we assume no outbound control plane. In that case central monitoring/analytics are delivered via an optional batched telemetry export on operator schedule (see runbook).
- If a secured egress tunnel is allowed we can enable near‑real‑time orchestration and reduce RTO for failover.

We will also include a short checklist for operator staffing / training and recommended DR test cadence. Attaching: redwood_private_sla_matrix.xlsx (SLA tiers + escalation contact paths) and operator-failover-runbook.pdf (procedural playbook).

If you want, Vanessa can outline licensing and DR drill coordination in a quick call.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Enterprise Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_private_sla_matrix.xlsx, operator-failover-runbook.pdf
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA / failover questions

Hi Alice —

Couple of procurement notes to call out so expectations match contractual language:

- Reserved capacity (99.95%) requires a monthly commitment and a defined maintenance window — we include two emergency maintenance days per year for critical security patches.
- Active/active: pricing tier depends on cross‑site data egress and replication throughput — we can provide a sizing estimate once we have your projected TPS and sequence length distribution.
- DR drills: we recommend annual operator‑led DR test (we can facilitate a dry‑run) — cost for Redwood‑led exercises is typically billed as professional services.

Happy to join the technical session to walk procurement teams through how the SLA maps to credits and remediation.

—Vanessa
Director, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA / failover questions

Alice —

From an implementation POV a few additional technical clarifications that the architecture team asked for:

- For active/passive we use a cross‑site heartbeat over a lightweight control channel. If sites cannot establish a secure control channel we fall back to manual promotion steps documented in the runbook.
- Cache warming: our KV cache has an incremental warm strategy — in the event of failover a warming window of 5–30 minutes is typical if data volume fits SSD working set; longer if rebuilding from cold storage.
- Metrics and observability: we ship local Prometheus metrics and a compact telemetry bundle for manual export from air‑gapped sites; optional encrypted batched export when egress is allowed.

Irene/Vanessa — we should propose a 30‑minute technical workshop with Alice's architect team next week to walk through topologies and pricing impact.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
From: Alice Park <alice@lumenhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@lumenhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA / failover questions

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications before we schedule the workshop:

1) For air‑gapped sites where no control plane egress is permitted, is the operator failover process fully documented such that our L3 ops team can run it end‑to‑end without Redwood personnel?
2) Are there automated integrity checks post‑failover (consistency verification) in the runbook we can adopt?
3) For the reserved capacity SLA, will you provide a sample credit calculation table we can include in the contract?

If yes to 1 & 2 we can route this through legal and procurement. If not, we will need to include a funded support requirement.

Best,
Alice
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@lumenhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA / failover questions

Hi Alice —

Short answers: yes, yes, and yes — and I’ve attached the artifacts you can drop into the RFP binder.

- Operator autonomy: the operator‑failover‑runbook.pdf includes a step‑by‑step checklist, pre‑flight checks, post‑validation queries, and a runbook play checklist designed for L3 ops without Redwood personnel. We also provide an optional operator training engagement (two days) that many customers include in their purchase order.
- Post‑failover integrity checks: the runbook contains automated verification scripts (hash checks, sample inference assertions, and metrics baselines) that your ops team can run locally — everything is designed to be executed without outbound connectivity.
- Credit calculation: redwood_private_sla_matrix.xlsx contains the SLA tiers and sample credit table. We can include contract language in the next iteration; Vanessa will align on procurement phrasing.

Next steps: I’ll upload these artifacts to the HubSpot deal and share a short demo/test plan link so your architects can review. Proposed 30‑minute workshop slots next week: Tue 10/12 10:00–10:30 or Wed 10/13 14:00–14:30 PT — let me know which works and we’ll get it on the calendar.

Links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/ LN-2027-045 (materials uploaded), https://app.redwood.com/docs/private-deploy/failover-playbook

Thanks again —
Irene
Enterprise Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
